label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
statement_en: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.

hypotheses.name: fisher-ftns#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.

hypotheses.name: fisher-ftns#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.

hypotheses.name: fisher-ftns#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.
Corollary: mean fitness never decreases under fixed fitnesses.
assumed: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.
Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

sources: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)
The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

non_vacuity_witness.statement: a theorem from standard axioms whose hypotheses are plain inequalities or decidable checks on the inputs; no separate witness structure (see scope.kernelChecked)
